profile_headline: Working on Youth Empowerment Initiatives in India and Oman
post_content:
We don't talk about it as much as we talk about other diseases, but you'll be
shocked to know that 300 million people worldwide are suffering from
depression. Depression and bad mental health have been ignored as a serious
issue since ages. But, do you know, depression can also lead to death if it
gets worst? And as per reports from WHO, India is the most depressed country
in the world followed by China and USA. And it's depression which is the root
cause for all suicides. What do you think are the causes of rising depression
and mental health among people? What can we do to help people in depression?
It's a high time we build a friendly and kind environment around us. There's a
need of cultural shift in our lifestyle. Do we ever greet a stranger with whom
we get eye contact while traveling or walking or in a lift? I have seen people
traveling in public transport and flights who don't even utter a single word
to the person next seated throughout their journey from source to destination.
And we rarely smile when we aren't with our friends or known ones. I don't
know what keeps people rigid to start interaction, practice empathy and build
new friendship? Someone you ignore might need you to talk. Why to miss that
opportunity?

profile_headline: Founder | Solving mental health through volunteer-run alternatives to therapy | Social Entrepreneur | Impact 11K+
post_content:
I grew up absurdly lonely, a product of a turbulent childhood, surrounded by
the most broken of the world. I always felt like a misfit. Someone who longed
for a chance to belong. I still remember on the last day of school, someone
wrote on my shirt, "You're too weird. I hope you change or you'll not have
friends someday." So I chased this 'normal'. The pain and the loneliness
engulfed me whole until I was convinced. That, there was something wrong with
me. Finally, on February 19th, 2016, this abnormal anomaly tried to end his
life. Then, he went out to find people like him. He started an NGO to help
people like him. He met 1000's of people. Those who've been raped more than 32
times, products of divorced marriages, inter faith marriages, heartbreak, loss
of family, orphans, those sexually, emotionally, physically abused, he saw and
heard it all. He went on to save many many lives and asked for nothing in
return. People who wanted to kill themselves, those unhappy, those who were on
the verge of falling apart, people like him, the broken of the world. Took him
23 years to understand. Some people can't ever fit in. They're not meant to.
They can only stand out for that's all they've ever known to do. Agree?

profile_headline: Human | School Dropout | Founder of Simply Blood | Social Entrepreneur | LinkedIn Power Profile 2018 | TEDx Speaker
post_content:
REFUSAL I am happy to share that my US trip is not possible (atleast for next
few months), as my application for US visa has been refused by the United
States Embassy in Delhi. Now, you must be thinking, Why Happy? So let me share
my point on this. I have been trained to face refusals since my childhood. -I
faced refusal to get access to enter 5 star hotels but I made it at the age of
14. -I was refused to get job due to my low qualifications, but I made it to
work in leading position at one of the best educational groups. -I was refused
to get support to run Change With One Foundation but I kept hustling and we
are doing good. -Now I have been refused for visa but I am damn sure, there is
something better we are going to do. There was no plan for me to visit US, but
when I got invitation from Curt DeBerg, it was a matter of pride for me to be
a part of such event. Many people came to make my trip impactful by supporting
me. I wanted to thanks deep from my heart to Amit Chandra, Pradeep Reddy
Kandimalla, Kalepu Ravishekar and so many others. I thought to find
opportunity to solve one social issue in "The land of Opportunity". But I
think America don't deserve me right now, better luck next time America. :)
